title: Pope Leo XIV Confirms Visit to the Basilica of Guadalupe, but Has Not Yet Set the Date
author: SinEmbargo Staff
content:
_This article by SinEmbargo Staff originally appeared in the[November 3, 2026
edition of SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4898115/papa-leon-xiv-
confirma-visita-a-la-basilica-de-guadalupe-pero-aun-no-define-la-fecha/), an
independent Mexican digital news outlet._

**Mexico City, November 3 (SinEmbargo).—** [**Pope Leo
XIV**](https://www.sinembargo.mx/tag/papa-leon-xiv/) will visit the **Basilica
of Guadalupe** in **Mexico City (CdMx)** , although the date of his trip has
not yet been set, **María Montserrat Alvarado** , the **Vatican** ’s new head
of Communication, confirmed this Tuesday.

> The Holy Father is indeed going to go see Our Lady of Guadalupe.
>
> María Montserrat Alvarado, Vatican communications chief

The [Mexican official](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4897694/montserrat-alvarado-
mexicana-y-primera-mujer-laica-en-la-comunicacion-del-vaticano/) made the
statement during the presentation of the program for the pontiff’s upcoming
tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, scheduled for November 6 to 17.

Alvarado explained that she will be “the first to announce Leo XIV’s trip to
Mexico,” which will mark her tenure after taking office on November 1 as the
first laywoman to head the Holy See’s press office.

Although the trip does not yet have a date on the calendar, the confirmation
reveals the pontiff’s intention to go to Mexico’s main Marian shrine, one of
the most important centers of Catholic pilgrimage in the world.

> [Post by @VaticanNews on
> X](https://twitter.com/VaticanNews/status/2117685742486925447)

## Leo XIV Could Visit Mexico During a Trip to the US

The possibility of the Pope coming to Mexican territory had already been
mentioned by Archbishop Paul Richard Gallagher, the Holy See’s Secretary for
Relations with States.

Last week, during a meeting with foreign journalists, Gallagher said that Leo
XIV plans to travel to the United States “in the not-too-distant future” and
that he is considering making a stop in Mexico to visit the shrine of the
Virgin of Guadalupe.

This possibility opens the door to both destinations being part of the same
tour of North America, although the Vatican has not yet confirmed an itinerary
or a schedule for the trip.

The trip would also come after President Claudia Sheinbaum extended him a
formal invitation to visit the country, a gesture that coincided with the wish
Leo XIV himself has expressed on other occasions to see the Basilica of
Guadalupe, a place of deep value for millions of believers.

![The Basilica of Guadalupe in Mexico City](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/11/02-basilica-guadalupe.jpg)The Basilica of Guadalupe is
one of the main Catholic pilgrimage centers in the world. Photo: X @SeGobCDMX

## The Pope Really Wants to Come: Sheinbaum

The news will be well received by millions of faithful, after President
Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo shared in early August that the Vatican Secretary of
State, Pietro Parolin, had informed her that Pope Leo XIV would not visit
Mexico during his tour of Latin America (LA) in November, but that he really
wanted to visit the country on another occasion.

> “Although obviously he could not come to Mexico during the electoral period,
> we continue to extend the invitation to him. They told us that he really
> wants to come to Mexico and that, in any case, they would be looking at the
> date when he could come. There is still no set date,” she said during her
> morning press conference on August 8.

In that regard, she recalled that the inclusion of Uruguay and Argentina on
the route had been planned from the beginning, since they are nations that
Francis was unable to visit during his pontificate, but with today’s
announcement, Leo XIV’s presence in Mexico is finally confirmed and all that
remains is to set the official date on the calendar.
